subject: environmental-science
title: Impact Prediction Methods
welcome_lead: Matrices, networks, GIS overlays — toolkits to forecast environmental change.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on impact prediction techniques.
final_note: Every prediction carries uncertainty — communicate it transparently.

walkthroughs.body_html: Leopold matrices use 8800 cells (100 actions × 88 components). Cells score magnitude and importance.
Network diagrams reveal cascading impacts — e.g., road → noise → wildlife displacement → ecotourism revenue.
Ian McHarg's overlay technique (1969) underlies modern GIS suitability analysis for site selection.

mcqs.q: How does the Brundtland Report define sustainable development?
options: Meeting present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs.
Stopping all development immediately.
Decomposition.
Environmental protection at all costs.

mcqs.q: What process moves carbon from the atmosphere into plants?
options: Photosynthesis.
Respiration.
Richness is for plants, evenness for animals.
Decomposition.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between species richness and species evenness?
options: Decomposition.
Richness is for plants, evenness for animals.
They are the same measurement.
Richness counts how many species exist; evenness measures how balanced their abundances are.
